llm.summary: The skill is mostly a normal WidgetKit review guide, but it requires an unbundled parent-directory protocol that can suppress review findings.

dimensions.detail: The skill asks the agent to inspect relevant WidgetKit source files during review, which fits the purpose, but the external protocol dependency broadens effective instructions beyond the packaged artifact.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains only Markdown files with no executable scripts, install hooks, dependencies, or network-loaded payloads.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: artifact/SKILL.md requires satisfying ../review-verification-protocol/SKILL.md before reporting and says to omit findings if that protocol is not satisfied; that external parent-directory instruction source is not included in the artifact and is not pinned or verifiable here.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, privilege escalation, background worker, credential harvesting, memory writes, or local system modification behavior was found in the inspected files.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review the external protocol dependency before installing. The WidgetKit guidance itself is ordinary documentation, but the skill should ideally bundle or pin the full verification checklist and avoid letting a missing or mutable sibling file suppress valid findings.
llm.findings:
[PE3] expected: The referenced Keychain text in references/performance.md is platform guidance saying Keychain can fail for widgets and to use App Groups instead; it does not load credential files or instruct credential access.
[T01] unexpected: The artifact-backed concern is the mandatory link from artifact/SKILL.md to an unbundled ../review-verification-protocol/SKILL.md with authority to block findings; this is a real review-integrity risk, not evidence of malware or system compromise.
